results.content: University of California San Francisco. # Urmimala Sarkar, MD, MPH. Urmimala Sarkar MD, MPH is Associate Chair for Faculty Experience for the Department of Medicine, Professor of Medicine at UCSF in the Division of General Internal Medicine, Associate Director of the UCSF Center for Vulnerable Populations, and a primary care physician at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital’s Richard H. Dr. Sarkar’s work centers on innovating for health equity and improving safety and quality of outpatient care for everyone, especially low-income and diverse populations. Her expertise spans topics including medical errors and patient safety, diabetes, and cancer prevention and survivorship. Dr. Sarkar’s research is collaborative and intersects with methods found in human centered design, human factors engineering, data science, health services research, and implementation science. Dr. Sarkar's research focuses on: (1) Ambulatory patient safety, (2) Digital health innovations to improve the safety and quality of outpatient care, (3) Social media research for behavior change,  (4) Safety-net implementation of evidence-based digital health in real-world settings.

results.content: Keywords: laboratory error, pre-analytical, analytical, post-analytical, patient safety, quality improvement Introduction Laboratory testing is integral to healthcare, informing 70-80% of medical diagnoses and guiding treatment decisions. While most errors are minor, some lead to inappropriate treatment, delayed care, and patient harm (Abdollahi, Saffar, & Saffar, 2014) Causes of laboratory errors are multifactorial, including high testing volumes, staffing shortages, complex diagnostic technology, and fragmented communication between laboratory and clinical teams. This review will examine the types, frequency, and causes of errors in laboratory testing and provide an overview of quality improvement strategies to enhance accuracy and patient safety. Databases such as PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched using keywords related to laboratory errors, including "pre-analytical," "analytical," and "post-analytical" errors, as well as "patient safety" and "quality improvement" in a laboratory setting. (2014) highlight that pre-analytical errors, including specimen misidentification and improper sample handling, account for the majority of laboratory errors, necessitating stringent control measures during the initial stages of the testing process. The post-analytical phase accounts for up to 47% of laboratory errors (Sadiq et al., 2014). Frequency and Impact of Laboratory Errors Studies show that the vast majority of laboratory errors occur in the pre-analytical and post-analytical phases, rather than the analytical testing itself. Reducing laboratory errors requires a focus on improving quality management in the extra-analytical phases (Carraro & Plebani, 2007; Mario Plebani, 2010). Pre-analytical Phase Errors The pre-analytical phase is a critical stage in the laboratory testing process where the majority of errors occur due to the complex nature of specimen collection and handling, involving various steps and personnel. Post-analytical Phase Errors The post-analytical phase involves reviewing, interpreting, reporting, and clinical actions based on laboratory test results. While the evolution of laboratory practices, particularly through automation and improved quality control measures, has mitigated the frequency of analytical errors, the pre-analytical and post-analytical phases continue to be vulnerable to mistakes. Title: Laboratory Errors: Causes, Types & Prevention Strategies
Laboratory Errors: Causes, Consequences and Prevention. ## **What Are** **Laboratory Errors****?**. In this blog, we will delve into the multifaceted world of laboratory errors, as well as explore comprehensive prevention strategies to help foster a culture of safety and excellence in lab practices. **Types of Errors in Laboratory** **Testing****. Errors in clinical laboratory are commonly categorized into three phases: pre-analytical, analytical, and post-analytical. Common lab errors in the pre-analytical phase include patient misidentification… incorrect sample collection… and delays in processing each of which can compromise sample integrity. Research indicates that a significant portion of clinical laboratory errors, between 60% to 70%, occur in the pre-analytical phase. Laboratory Errors: Pre-Analytical, Analytical & Post-Analytical. Laboratory Errors: Pre-Analytical, Analytical & Post-Analytical. Common laboratory errors can significantly affect patient care and outcomes. The categories that cause most laboratory errors include human factors, systemic issues, and technological factors. Human factors encompass traits and conditions that may lead to laboratory errors, like:. A robust quality management system (QMS) is crucial in minimizing laboratory errors by standardizing procedures and ensuring consistent adherence to laboratory best practices. Consequences of Common Laboratory Errors**. Laboratory errors can have severe implications for patient safety, financial stability, and the vital trust between healthcare providers and patients. Laboratory errors, such as incorrect test results or mislabelling of samples, can lead to misdiagnosis—a critical issue that may result in inappropriate treatment and adverse patient outcomes. Medical laboratory errors can erode trust between clinicians, patients, and healthcare institutions. How to Reduce Laboratory Errors: Prevention Strategies?**. To mitigate common laboratory errors and enhance overall patient safety, medical labs must implement effective prevention strategies that encompass quality management, employee training, technological integration, and a culture of reporting errors in the lab. The challenges of laboratory errors extend far beyond mere statistical anomalies; they strike at the heart of patient care, the lab’s reputation, and the financial viability of healthcare systems. From fostering a culture of open error reporting to embracing technological innovations that enhance accuracy, medical laboratories can adapt preventive strategies to significantly reduce risks, sharpen accuracy, and enhance patient care. While being mindful of all these aspects, laboratories can seamlessly transform into error-free environments that ensure the highest standards of care are met for every patient.
